Article Title: Airlines warn of diplomatic fallout over slot cuts
Article Text:
West Asia Carriers Allege Discrimination (Pic Credit: ANI)

MUMBAI: Some foreign airlines facing relocation from Mumbai airport have threatened reciprocal measures under bilateral air services agreements if Mumbai International Airport Ltd (MIAL) denies them historical slots for the summer 2027 schedule. Last week, MIAL decided to cut slots for airlines serving 14 destinations as part of a capacity-reduction plan linked to T1 redevelopment. The move has disproportionately affected West Asian carriers.Four airlines have written separately to MIAL and the ministry of civil aviation (MoCA), escalating the dispute to diplomatic channels, said sources. The carriers have sought MoCA intervention and warned of escalation to the govt, Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) and aviation authorities in their respective countries, including possible reciprocal measures under bilateral agreements.They have questioned why flights to 14 international destinations, mostly in West Asia, were selected for relocation from T2. One letter called the move "highly discriminatory and targeted towards" West Asia markets", while excluding Dubai and Abu Dhabi without justification. The 14 destinations are Bahrain, Dammam, Dhaka, Doha, Fujairah, Jakarta, Jeddah, Kathmandu, Kuwait City, Madinah, Muscat, Ras Al Khaimah, Riyadh and Sharjah.The airlines have also questioned the regulatory basis and methodology for the capacity cut, seeking a copy of any MoCA approval for the cited 5 million passengers per annum reduction and denial of historical slots. Arguing that redevelopment cannot override established historical slot entitlements, they asked: "On what authority does MIAL propose to decline summer 2027 historical slots?" They have demanded written confirmation that their S27 slots will be honoured without unilateral reduction or cancellation.MIAL's capacity-reduction plan is linked to the redevelopment of Terminal 1, which will eventually require passenger traffic to be redistributed between Mumbai and Navi Mumbai airports. tnn
Article Summary: Four airlines have written separately to MIAL and the ministry of civil aviation. MIAL decided to cut slots for airlines serving 14 destinations as part of a capacity-reduction plan linked to T1 redevelopment. The move has disproportionately affected West Asian carriers. The carriers have sought MoCA intervention and warned of escalation.

Article Title: Magnitude 4 earthquake strikes Assam's Kamrup district
Article Text:
Assam earthquake reports no immediate damage

This is a developing story.

NEW DELHI: An earthquake of magnitude 4.0 struck Assam's Kamrup district on Saturday afternoon.According to the National Center for Seismology (NCS), the earthquake occurred at 2:43:05 pm IST, at a depth of 10 km. The epicentre was located at latitude 25.749° North and longitude 91.273° East in Kamrup, Assam.In its X post, the NCS shared the seismic details, confirming the magnitude, time, depth and location of the earthquake.There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage.
Article Summary: An earthquake of magnitude 4.0 struck Assam's Kamrup district on Saturday afternoon. There were no immediate reports of casualties or damage. The epicentre was located at latitude 25.749° North and longitude 91.273° East in Kamrup, Assam.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor appeared to take a swipe at the controversy over errors in Sonia Gandhi 's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, after drawing attention to a typo in his own social media post about the Bharat Summit. Tharoor, who had mistakenly written #BgaratSummit while sharing a video of his speech at the event, later apologised and corrected the hashtag. He subsequently shared a link to an interview and review of Sonia Gandhi's book, captioning it: "A couple of typos are being fixed online!"In a post on X, Tharoor acknowledged the error in his earlier post and said he was unable to edit it."Apologies, unable to edit the typo for some reason. Of course I meant the #BharatSummit!"The Congress MP had earlier shared a link to his full speech at the opening dinner of the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad on Thursday. However, the hashtag in his post appeared as #BgaratSummit instead of #BharatSummit.Soon after, Tharoor shared a separate post linking to an interview titled Sonia Gandhi, 'Belonging' And Why This Story Lies On Other Side Of Politics: my review of the book everyone is talking about. The post carried the caption, "A couple of typos are being fixed online!", in what appeared to be a reference to the discussion around errors in Sonia Gandhi's recently released memoir.Tharoor's post sharing the interview and referring to typos being fixed onlineSonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, was released in India on November 10. The book traces her childhood in post-war Italy, her relationship with former prime minister Rajiv Gandhi, her life in the Gandhi family and her experiences in Indian politics.The memoir has also drawn political reactions, with BJP leaders questioning several of Sonia Gandhi's accounts of key events, including the 1984 anti-Sikh riots, the Babri Masjid demolition, the Batla House encounter and the Emergency.BJP spokesperson CR Kesavan had criticised the book, saying it attempted to "whitewash" the historical wrongs of the Nehru-Gandhi family and the Congress. He also questioned Sonia Gandhi's account of her emotional responses to certain incidents and her references to the Emergency imposed by former prime minister Indira Gandhi.Tharoor's posts came amid the online discussion surrounding the memoir and his own typo in the Bharat Summit post.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor appeared to take a swipe at the controversy over errors in Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love. He drew attention to a typo in his own social media post about the Bharat Summit. The Congress MP had mistakenly written #BgaratSummit while sharing a video of his speech at the event.

Article Title: 'Discussions ended the day he left us': Supriya Sule breaks silence on NCP merger buzz
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Nationalist Congress Party (SP) working president and MP Supriya Sule on Saturday said discussions over a possible merger between the two rival NCP factions had come to an end following the death of her brother and former Maharashtra deputy chief minister Ajit Pawar Her remarks come amid speculation over a possible reunion between the factions led by Sharad Pawar and Ajit Pawar, with leaders from both sides now ruling out any immediate merger.Speaking at a presser, Sule said, "The merger (of both factions of the party) was discussed until my brother (Ajit Pawar) was alive. The day he left us, it put a full stop to those discussions."Ajit Pawar died on January 28, 2026 after the aircraft carrying him crashed while attempting to land at Baramati airport in Pune district.Meanwhile, Maharashtra NCP president and MP Sunil Tatkare on Friday also dismissed speculation about a possible merger, asserting that his faction was not considering any reunion with the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SCP).“There is absolutely no discussion regarding a merger in our party at any level,” Tatkare told news agency ANI.Speculation over a possible reunion intensified after senior NCP leader Praful Patel recently met Sharad Pawar.However, Tatkare described the meeting as a personal visit to enquire about the veteran leader's health, dismissing any political significance.“Pawar Sahab has contributed to national politics for 60 years. At 86, his health hasn't been well. We have all reached various political positions with his blessings. Praful Bhai simply went to check on his health,” he said.Reaffirming his faction's association with the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA), Tatkare said, “We joined the NDA after deep consideration under the leadership of Narendra Modi. We are in the NDA and will remain in the NDA."Tatkare also hit back at Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut over his recent claim that 20 to 22 MLAs were ready to switch sides.“After the assembly elections, his mental health has deteriorated. Mentally, he is not fit. These statements are completely baseless,” he said.Tatkare further asserted that his faction would remain with the NDA under the leadership of Sunetra Pawar, adding that the "question of a merger does not even arise."Clarifying his earlier remarks on the merger discussions, Tatkare said there was "no confusion" on his part. He maintained that late Ajit Pawar, whom party leaders referred to as 'Dada', had spoken to him in detail about a possible merger on February 12 and had even outlined a formula for the arrangement after the proposed reunion.
Article Summary: Nationalist Congress Party (SP) working president and MP Supriya Sule said discussions over a possible merger between the two rival NCP factions had come to an end following the death of her brother Ajit Pawar. Sule: "The merger (of both factions of the party) was discussed until my brother (Ajit Pawar) was alive. The day he left us, it put a full stop to those discussions"

Article Title: Mekedatu Dam row: Stalin seeks united Tamil Nadu stand, asks Vijay to call all-party meeting
Article Text:
Stalin asks Vijay government not to remain silent on Mekedatu project

Stalin proposes joint meeting with PM Modi

Shivakumar says Karnataka will protect its right to build dam

NEW DELHI: DMK chief and former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin on Saturday urged chief minister Joseph Vijay to convene an all-party meeting to discuss Karnataka 's proposed Mekedatu dam project, calling for a united political response to protect the state's Cauvery water rights and the livelihood of its farmers.In a letter dated November 14, Stalin referred to Karnataka deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar 's recent remarks that no one could stop the construction of the proposed dam.Shivakumar made the statement at a government function in Mysuru on Friday in the presence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi .Sharing the letter on X, Stalin said Karnataka's position on the project required a response from the Tamil Nadu government. He described the Cauvery issue as a matter of "life and death" for the state and urged Vijay's government not to remain silent."Beyond mere water sharing, Cauvery is historically and emotionally intertwined with the lives of Tamils. The entire livelihood of delta farmers depends upon it," Stalin wrote.He said political parties in Karnataka were speaking in one voice on the Cauvery issue and argued that Tamil Nadu's parties should also demonstrate unity. Stalin had previously called for an all-party meeting to discuss the state's next steps, he said."Given the situation where the Karnataka Chief Minister has once again begun speaking aggressively about building the Mekedatu dam, the Government of Tamil Nadu must no longer remain silent. Therefore, I request through this letter that an all-party meeting be convened to express our unity and opposition to the Karnataka chief minister's statements," he wrote.Stalin also proposed that leaders of legislative parties in Tamil Nadu and all-party MPs jointly meet Prime Minister Modi to present the state's position.He said they should submit the resolutions adopted at the proposed all-party meeting, along with a unanimous resolution passed by the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly against the Mekedatu project in June, directly to the Prime Minister."Regarding Cauvery rights, it is essential that we stand united, transcending personal likes and dislikes as well as party differences," Stalin said.The DMK leader also questioned reports that Vijay was planning to visit Karnataka for discussions on the Cauvery issue. He reiterated that Tamil Nadu's position had consistently been to secure its water rights through legal means rather than negotiations with Karnataka.Stalin said the state had previously warned against such a visit, quoting his earlier message to Vijay: "Do not run into this disaster."He also cited Shivakumar's remarks that it was the Tamil Nadu government which had sought talks, not Karnataka, and that the Tamil Nadu chief minister did not need to visit the neighbouring state under the present circumstances.The latest exchange follows Shivakumar's remarks on Friday, when he said Karnataka would protect its right to build the Mekedatu balancing reservoir and release 177 thousand million cubic feet (TMC) of water to Tamil Nadu as required by law.Shivakumar said the Supreme Court had already passed an order on the issue and that the next step was to secure the necessary clearances. He said he had sought forest and environmental approvals from the Centre."Mekedatu issue - Supreme Court has given order. Now what we need is just one thing - all parties have agreed, let's go together. For that, I am sending everything - forest clearance, environment clearance. I have asked for one forest clearance and one environment clearance," he said.Shivakumar maintained that building the dam was Karnataka's right and invited Tamil Nadu representatives to visit and understand how the project would benefit the state."It is my state, my right. And they [Tamil Nadu] should also know; Tamil Nadu also should know. Let them come with the delegation; I will show them, I will explain to them how it helps them," he said.He added that he had told the Centre he would bring an all-party delegation to press for the project and that the proposal had been accepted.The Mekedatu project envisages a balancing reservoir on the Cauvery river in Karnataka, primarily to meet Bengaluru's drinking water needs and generate hydroelectric power. Tamil Nadu has consistently opposed it, citing concerns over the availability of Cauvery water for downstream areas, particularly its agricultural delta districts.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu chief minister MK Stalin calls for a united political response to protect the state's Cauvery water rights and the livelihood of its farmers. Stalin referred to Karnataka deputy chief minister DK Shivakumar's recent remarks that no one could stop the construction of the proposed dam. Shivak Kumar said the Supreme Court had already passed an order on the issue.

Article Title: Godhra train fire was deliberate, Sonia Gandhi's memoir claim is wrong: Ex-CBI officer
Article Text:
File photo

Belonging: A Journey of Love

Asthana says SIT re-examined Gujarat Police investigation

Nanavati Commission and Banerjee Committee reached different conclusions

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

59 people killed in Sabarmati Express fire

NEW DELHI: Former CBI special director Rakesh Asthana , who led the Gujarat Police investigation into the 2002 Godhra train burning , has rejected a passage in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir describing the cause of the fire as "disputed", maintaining that the investigation and subsequent court proceedings established that it was deliberately set.In an interview with news agency ANI, Asthana said investigators had examined different theories and possibilities before collecting evidence that connected the accused to the crime.He argued that the findings had been upheld by the Nanavati Commission, a Supreme Court-appointed Special Investigation Team (SIT) and the courts.Reacting to the passage in Gandhi's memoir,, Asthana said, "That is completely wrong, the investigation is authentic. It has been proved in the court of law. Even now, if someone is creating doubt about it, then it is for political reasons; there can be no other explanation for it."Sonia writes in her memoir, "The riots were triggered when four coaches of the Sabarmati Express were set on fire and 59 pilgrims died. The train was returning to the state capital Ahmedabad from Ayodhya, carrying Hindu karsevaks, volunteers for the Ram temple.The cause of the fire remains disputed, but the turmoil that followed spread to many parts of the state."Asked whether the doubts were being raised for vote-bank politics, Asthana said the investigation had treated the deaths as a criminal matter, irrespective of the victims' religion."All the people who died in Godhra were Hindus. And whoever's death it may be—whether a Hindu's, a Muslim's, a Christian's, or a Sikh's—death is death, murder is murder. So we investigated it as a criminal act. But unfortunately, the issue was made out in such a way that an attempt was made to investigate the case to benefit Mr. Modi," he said.Asthana said the Gujarat Police's investigation, which began with the CID Crime unit and continued until 2008, was subsequently examined in detail by a Supreme Court-appointed SIT headed by then CBI Director RK Raghavan.He said the Supreme Court constituted the team in 2008, with former Uttar Pradesh director General of Police CB Satpathy also part of the investigation. Satpathy headed the SIT in Raghavan's absence, Asthana said.The team re-examined the entire investigation, visited the site and questioned the officers who had conducted the original probe."They examined the entire investigation again. In fact, they examined us as well. We explained to them what investigation we had carried out. They visited the site and examined everything. They then concluded that they could not find any flaw in the investigation conducted by the Gujarat Police," Asthanan said.He said Raghavan and Satpathy submitted their findings to the Supreme Court, which accepted the report. The subsequent trial proceeded on the basis of the investigation, leading to convictions in 2011, he added.Asthana also cited the findings of the Nanavati Commission, constituted by the Gujarat government in 2002 to investigate the Godhra incident and the communal riots that followed.He said the commission, initially headed by Justice KG Shah before Justice Nanavati was appointed in May 2002, examined the train burning and the subsequent riots separately. Its report on the Godhra incident, submitted in 2008, concluded that the fire was part of a pre-planned conspiracy and had been deliberately set, he said.According to Asthana, around 44,000 affidavits were submitted before the commission and more than 1,000 witnesses were examined.He contrasted these findings with those of the committee headed by Justice UC Banerjee, which was constituted by then Railway Minister Lalu Prasad Yadav in 2004. The committee concluded that the fire was accidental and suggested that a stove carried in the karsevaks' coach had caused it, Asthana said.He added that the Banerjee Committee's report was challenged before the Gujarat High Court, which held that the committee was illegal because a commission under the Commission of Inquiry Act was already examining the incident. Asthana said the report was subsequently set aside."The fact is that the investigation established that the fire was deliberate. The commission established it, the Supreme Court-appointed SIT established it, and the courts convicted the accused on the basis of the same evidence," he said.On February 27, 2002, coach S-6 of the Sabarmati Express caught fire near Godhra railway station in Gujarat, killing 59 people, including women and children. The train was carrying Hindu karsevaks returning from Ayodhya.The incident was followed by communal violence in several parts of Gujarat, in which hundreds of people were killed.In 2011, a special court convicted 31 people in connection with the train burning. The Gujarat High Court in 2014 upheld the convictions of 11 accused while acquitting 20 others.The Supreme Court subsequently upheld the Gujarat High Court's verdict and dismissed appeals filed by the convicts in the case.
Article Summary: Former CBI special director Rakesh Asthana led the Gujarat Police investigation into the 2002 Godhra train burning. He rejected a passage in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir describing the cause of the fire as "disputed" He said the investigation and subsequent court proceedings established that it was deliberately set.

Article Title: 'Jewel of India': PM Modi, Rahul Gandhi, Rajnath Singh pay tributes to Nehru on birth anniversary
Article Text:
Rahul remembers Nehru as 'jewel of India' (Picture from X handle of Supriya Shrinate)

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on his 137th birth anniversary, which is also observed as Children's Day across the country.In a post on X, PM Modi said, "Paying tribute to former PM Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary."Defence minister Rajnath Singh also paid homage to the country's first prime minister, recalling his contribution to India's freedom struggle and his leadership during the early years of independent India.In a post on X, Rajnath said, "On the birth anniversary of Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru Ji, I pay my tributes to him. His contribution to India’s freedom struggle and his leadership as the first Prime Minister of independent India left an enduring imprint on the formative years of our nation."Lok Sabha leader of opposition and former Congress chief Rahul Gandhi also paid tribute to Jawaharlal Nehru on his birth anniversary.In a post on X, Rahul described Nehru as the "jewel of India" and the country's first prime minister.He said freedom was not the destination but "a milestone in the nation's new journey", adding that Swaraj was not merely about power but about every citizen's participation and responsibility towards the country's future.Rahul also recalled Nehru's vision of India as an idea built on diversity, democracy and equality."Their dream of a modern, scientific, progressive, and self-confident India remains our inspiration today," he said, adding that efforts to build such an India would be the "true tribute" to Nehru.November 14 is celebrated as Children's Day in India to mark the birth anniversary of Nehru, who was popularly known as 'Chacha Nehru' because of his affection for children.After Nehru's death, it was unanimously decided to observe his birthday as ' Bal Diwas ' or Children's Day in India. He was born on November 14, 1889, in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh, and died on May 27, 1964.Nehru became India's first prime minister on August 15, 1947, after playing an active role in the country's freedom struggle.Schools across the country organise various activities for students on the occasion, including games and competitions. Government bodies also pay tribute to the former prime minister and hold commemorative events.The United Nations declared November 20 as Universal Children's Day in 1954. India initially observed Children's Day on the same date.However, following Nehru's death in 1964, Parliament unanimously passed a resolution to mark his birth anniversary on November 14 as National Children's Day.
Article Summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday paid tribute to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru on his 137th birth anniversary. Defence minister Rajnath Singh also paid homage to the country's first prime minister. November 14 is celebrated as Children's Day in India to mark the birth anniversary of Nehru.

After surrendering in Feb 2026 and enrolling in a law college, top CPI(Maoist) leader Thippiri Thirupathi alias Deoji, 61, is ready for his next innings in democratic politics. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoist) and make it a lawful, people-centric party. Excerpts:Also read - 'From armed struggle to people's politics': Ex-Maoist leader Deoji outlines new path, seeks release of jailed cadres I left studies and shifted to Dandkarenya forests in 1984. The socio-political scenario in those times was marked by exploitation of peasantry and women by feudalistic set-up, both in urban and rural settings. In 1978, there was a big uprising by the farmers of Telangana and a declaration was made to fight against oppression and agitate for people's rights. There was mass mobilisation and a people’s movement started to give voice to farmers, women and the weaker sections. Starting from Karimnagar, it soon spread across Telangana. I was then following this movement closely and subscribed to its anti-feudal sentiment; I joined the students' Radical Students Union (RSU) to actively 'support this cause. I was arrested several times and tortured by the police. Since circumstances did not allow us to carry out our struggle in the open, I had to go underground.Our commitment to CPI(Maoist)’s agenda of seizing power through armed revolution, had mentally prepared us to face all odds and hardships. As we continued working, our resolve only strengthened...so negotiating difficult terrain, exhaustion, poor living conditions felt normal to us.There were three sources. Firstly, we would snatch or loot weapons (from the security forces); secondly, we manufactured weapons on our own. Thirdly, depending on the funds available, we also purchased arms and ammunition from the domestic arms dealers and smugglers. We have never secured weapons from anti-India, foreign-based sources in lieu of furthering their agenda.CPI(Maoist) was mostly funded by the people after we explained to them the political cause behind waging an armed struggle and the need for weapons. Also, we extorted money from outsiders who worked in our area; like tendu patta contractors and bamboo harvesters. But we steered clear of contractors engaged in construction of roads or bridges as we believe they exploit our resources. That CPI(Maoist) had massive funds is propaganda. Our policy is to raise money to sustain us for the next three years. This money is spent on people’s issues, armed struggle and propaganda; extravagance is strictly avoided. The party never had funds in excess of Rs 30-40 crore at any time. These would largely be exhausted after fulfilling needs for the current year; only a little would be carried over to the second year. There were never any funds for the third year.After People's War merged with MCC in 2004 to form the CPI(Maoist), then PM Manmohan Singh had declared Naxalism as the biggest internal security challenge facing the country. Thereafter, the entire govt machinery -- the Centre, affected states, intelligence agencies, Central para-military forces etc -- drafted a national policy to eradicate Naxalism. This unified, coordinated fight against Naxalism peaked in 2025. Security operations were only a part of this multi-pronged counter-Naxal approach, which also focused on a development of connectivity push in the affected areas. Many Naxals leaders, cadres and PLGA commanders were arrested or killed; we also lost our general secretary Namballa Keshav Rao in 2025. This weakened the CPI(Maoist) both quantitatively and qualitatively. Its geographical area of influence shrunk. We no longer had the capability to resist the security forces. Our weapons were seized. In view of our dwindling numbers, leadership, weaponry and area of influence, our movement suffered a massive setback.In Dec 2023, at an all-India conference of DGPs chaired by HM Amit Shah, consensus emerged in favour of waging a decisive battle to eliminate Naxalism. Operation Kagaar was launched in Jan 2024 and continued till March 2026.In Aug 2024, our PB/CC members met in Dandakaranya, We assessed that the decline in Naxals’ influence that began in 2018 had acquired serious proportions. We decided to disband the big outfits like PLGA, operate in small teams and work amongst the people. The cadres were incapable of implementing these decisions. It became too much of a security risk for them to move out of Dandakaranya. They had to concentrate there, exposing themselves to the forces that had encircled the area. We paid a heavy price as we could not operationalise the tactical decisions of Aug 2024.In March 2025, we decided that we were open to holding peace talks with the govt. Our condition was cessation of operations against us. But the Central govt rejected peace talks. The anti-Naxal operations continued with severity and many of our top leaders, including general secretary Nambala Keshav Rao, were killed. This crushed our movement. After Sonu surrendered, which was not cleared by PB, we could not arrest the wave of surrenders.Had the coordinated and fierce operations by the Centre and 12 states against CPI(Maoist) not been run with a definite deadline, our movement would have lasted longer as the people’s issues we raise remain relevant even today — loot by corporates in tribal areas and feudal oppression.Given the circumstances we did some rethinking and concluded that the situation was no longer conducive to continuing the armed struggle. So we decided to give up violence and come overground. We have not surrendered to lead a comfortable personal life. We want to take up people’s issues through legal means. We will now engage in people’s politics to achieve an oppression and exploitation-free society.We have been demanding that the ban on CPI(Maoist) should be lifted. This way we can take up political activity in an open and legal manner. Even the ban on our frontal outfits must go as there has been no violent incident from our side over the past 8-10 months.It is also our responsibility to secure the release of Maoist cadres languishing in prisons. This is our demand before the Centre and state govts. HM Amit Shah claims the country became Naxal-free in March 2026; so it is only apt to free Naxals who are still in jails. They cannot go back to violence when freed, as they don't have weapons. We welcome the govt’s decision to review cases against Naxals and free those jailed for non-serious crimes. But a distinction must not be drawn between serious and non-serious crimes. Govt may argue that the Maoists have killed many people, including police personnel, and that law should take its course. But this was a war and war always results in losses on both sides. After war, peace must be established. 6000-7000 Maoists are in jail; a blanket govt order must be issued for their release.Our third demand is leniency for the 10 Maoists given death sentence for the Jhiram Ghati attack case. Our demand for blanket release of Maoists should cover them as well.Our fourth demand is to extend protection to surrendered Naxals in Chhattisgarh against revenge attacks.Politics does not exist in a rigid form. Unlike Vedas, Puranas etc that are divine scriptures and cannot be rewritten, politics is dynamic. Politics must adapt to the changing times, be it the evolving national and international situation or objective and subjective conditions; political documents cannot be construed as eternal truth. Leninism and Marxism may be our theory, but the political document must be rewritten to reflect changed tactics and strategy.We will need to consult the other leaders as well as cadres of CPI(Maoist) on whether or not to join electoral politics. If the assessment is that elections will not achieve our ends, we may stay away.Since Shah had asked us to work openly and legally, our obvious choice is to do so through CPI(Maoist). We will wait and watch and take a call on alternatives if this does not work out.As we engage in political activity as per law, we shall need a network of legal experts across the country to implement our political agenda efficiently. The knowledge of law will help us to comment and correctly interpret the law to defend activities that are within the legal framework. It will also help in perception management.Armed struggle cannot be carried on or stopped with an edict or order. Popular sentiment decides its fate. Objective conditions create popular sentiment…which then takes the form of a call to the masses and congregation. This is how people’s movements are made. Nobody can predict what will happen in the future. But we are reiterating that after embracing a life in the open, we will carry out our political agenda only within the boundaries of the Constitution and law.
Article Summary: Former supreme commander and General Secretary of the banned CPI (Maoist), Thippiri Tirupathi, also known as Deoji, addresses media during a meeting with party leaders, in Hyderabad. Deoji speaks to TOI's Bharti Jain on his demand to lift the ban on CPI(Maoists) and make it a lawful, people-centric party.

Article Title: Indonesian woman with alleged Chinese links caught at Sonauli border after failing to speak Hindi

LUCKNOW: An Indonesian woman, who allegedly posed as a Kolkata resident using forged Indian identity documents and claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China, was caught by bureau of immigration officials at the Sonauli border in Maharajganj district after she was unable to speak Hindi properly during questioning.The woman, identified as Rohana, was intercepted on Nov 10 while attempting to cross into Nepal. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. Her claimed association with a Kolkata-based NGO facilitating visits to China has emerged as a key aspect of the case.According to an FIR registered at Sonauli police station, the woman initially identified herself as Li Kim Lien, daughter of Li Chin Sen, and claimed to be a resident of New Tangra Road in Kolkata, West Bengal.The complaint lodged by immigration officer stated that the woman arrived at the Sonauli immigration office around 7.30 pm on Nov 10 and presented an Indian voter ID card bearing the number ZJJ2157469.The document identified her as Li Kim Lien, born on June 29, 1975, with a residential address at 8, New Tangra Road, under Kolkata Municipal Corporation, Tangra, Kolkata.However, immigration officials became suspicious when she was unable to speak Hindi properly.Her responses during questioning raised doubts about her claimed Indian identity, prompting officials to examine her passport.The passport, bearing number X2398351, identified her as Rohana, an Indonesian citizen born on Oct 20, 1970. It also showed that she possessed an Indian employment visa.The FIR states that she held an E-3 employment visa bearing number VL9126916, valid from Oct 11, 2025, to Nov 9, 2026. Her passport also contained details of a multiple-entry Indian visa issued on Aug 11, 2023.During questioning, the woman reportedly told immigration officials that she was working as president of an NGO based in Kolkata. She further claimed that the organisation provided technical assistance to Buddhist monks travelling to China.The FIR neither identifies the NGO nor specifies the nature of its activities or establishes any link with Chinese govt authorities."We are still in the initial stage of investigation to claim or deny if the woman was involved in espionage or any other activity beyond the alleged immigration and identity-document offences," an immigration official source said.According to the FIR, officials found that the woman possessed an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and PAN card in the name of Li Kim Lien, while another PAN card was issued in the name of Rohana.The FIR alleges that the woman had obtained Indian identity documents by changing her name and address despite being an Indonesian citizen.Police registered the case under Sections 319(2), 336(3), 338 and 340(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, relating to cheating by personation, forgery and use of forged documents, along with Sections 22 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025.
Article Summary: Indonesian woman held at Sonauli border with alleged forged Indian IDs. She was allegedly carrying an Indian voter ID card, Aadhaar card and two PAN cards bearing different names and conflicting dates of birth. She claimed to be president of an NGO assisting Buddhist monks travelling to China.

However, she alleged that her visa was cancelled shortly before she was due to leave for the airport, citing "orders from above" in the ministry of home affairs.Lyng's case has also drawn attention because of her earlier interaction with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his visit to Oslo in May. The Norwegian journalist had questioned PM Modi on press freedom and his reluctance to take questions from journalists during the visit.The reported visa cancellations have triggered a political row, with opposition leaders questioning the government's decision and alleging that foreign journalists and speakers were being prevented from attending the international gathering.Telangana CM A Revanth Reddy launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi, accusing him of having a dictatorial mindset over the alleged restrictions on foreign journalists attending the Bharat Summit.In a post on X, Reddy alleged that some journalists were stopped from entering India by the ministry of home Affairs despite having received visas. Questioning the reported action, he said, "Is asking Modi ji a question a crime? It is journalists' responsibility to ask questions. Trying to put us on the mat."Suggesting a tougher response, he added, "Our answer to this should be to tighten up grant of visas to Norwegian journalists."The BJP, meanwhile, defended the visa cancellations, branding the gathering an "Anti-Bharat Summit" and accusing the Congress of bringing together radical Left and anti-India groups.

Article Title: Women at the controls, solar power on the rooftops: What makes Pune Metro's Pink Line special
Article Text:
PM Modi virtually inaugurated Pune Metro's Pink Line on November 3 and commercial operations began the following day

Why Pune needed the Metro

Why the Pink Line matters

Pune Metro's Pink Line is the network's third corridor to open and the first to pass through Hinajwadi, the city's IT hub

Pune Metro's Pink Line: A timeline of the project

Women at the controls

What makes Pune Metro's Pink Line special

A Metro corridor powered partly by solar energy

Pune Metro's Pink Line in numbers

India's first Metro project under the 2017 Metro policy's PPP framework

Beyond Metro connectivity

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The way forward for Pune Metro's Pink Line

On November 3, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for Pune Metro projects worth around Rs 21,800 crore.The project he inaugurated was Line 3 of Pune Metro, popularly known as the Pink Line. Built at a cost of approximately Rs 8,300 crore, the 23.2-km corridor connects Maan, on Pune's northwestern outskirts, with the District Court Metro station in Shivajinagar, central Pune. Also known as Civil Court station, it serves as an interchange with Line 1 (Purple Line) and Line 2 (Aqua Line), connecting passengers to other parts of the Metro network.PM Modi described the Pink Line as "so special". Beyond the connectivity it offers, the corridor stands out for its distinctive approach to operations, infrastructure development and sustainability.Over the years, Pune's population has grown significantly, with people from other parts of Maharashtra as well as outside the state migrating to the city. Pune was home to over 12 lakh people in 1981, according to that year's national census. The figure rose to more than 31 lakh in 2011, the latest national census, meaning the city added around 19 lakh people in 30 years – an increase of nearly 160%.Migration to Pune and the subsequent population expansion have largely been driven by the growth of its IT, manufacturing and educational sectors.Pune is counted among India's leading IT hubs, alongside Bengaluru and Hyderabad. Several prominent colleges and universities are also located in the city, further contributing to its growing population and demand for public transport.Against this backdrop, the foundation stone for the first phase of Pune Metro, comprising the Purple and Aqua lines, was laid in December 2016. The network's commercial operations commenced in March 2022.Although the launch of Pune Metro improved connectivity, several important areas remained outside its network, limiting its reach. The Pink Line addresses part of this gap by connecting Hinjawadi to the existing Metro network.The significance of the Pink Line extends beyond it being just another corridor of the Pune Metro network. Before the route opened to the public on November 4, a day after its inauguration, the network had no connectivity to Hinjawadi, one of Pune's largest employment centres and a major IT hub. The area houses offices of major technology companies such as Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Wipro and Cognizant.The Purple Line, which runs between Pimpri-Chinchwad and Swargate, and the Aqua Line, connecting Vanaz and Ramwadi, were the only two operational corridors at the time. As a result, software professionals living in other parts of Pune had to rely on road transport to commute to Hinjawadi or relocate closer to their workplaces.With 17 of the corridor's stations now operational and the remaining six scheduled to open in March 2027, commuters can interchange at District Court station in Shivajinagar and travel directly to Hinjawadi, making daily commutes more seamless.Commuters have also expressed hope that the Pink Line will ease congestion on roads leading to Hinjawadi.“The entire stretch from Wakad to Hinjawadi Phase-II remains busy and chaotic during rush hours. We expect relief from these snarls,” a commuter told The Times of India in an earlier report.Another commuter, who travels by bike to his workplace at Balewadi near Hinjawadi, noted that the Metro journey took nearly as much time as his two-wheeler commute but offered greater comfort.“My travel time by bike would be around 30-45 minutes, depending on the traffic. It took about 30 minutes to reach Balewadi by Metro. There was no huge drop in the travel time, but the overall comfort in Metro was much more,” he added.Another important feature of the Pink Line, officials say, is its provision for last-mile connectivity through bus services, dedicated pickup zones for taxis and auto-rickshaws, and cycle parking at stations.With the Pink Line now open, the Aqua and Purple lines being expanded, and a fourth corridor taking shape, the focus will increasingly be on integrating the expanding Metro network with other transport modes to improve connectivity across Pune.In October 2011, a woman loco pilot, Priyanka N, drove the inaugural train of Namma Metro in Bengaluru. Since then, several Metro networks across the country have employed women as train operators.However, Pune has taken this a step further by introducing an entire Metro corridor where all train drivers are women.While other Metro networks in India, including Delhi and Bengaluru, also have corridors designated as the Pink Line, Pune's newest Metro corridor has a special significance attached to the name. Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said the corridor would be called the Pink Line because its trains would be operated exclusively by women.Nearly 15 years after Priyanka N drove the first Namma Metro train, Pune Metro's Pink Line has become India's first Metro corridor to have an all-women team of train drivers.As many as 90 women have completed training and obtained competency certificates to operate trains on the Hinjawadi–Shivajinagar route. Recruited through campus drives, they underwent classroom instruction, practical sessions and extensive on-track training before being cleared to operate passenger services. The women have since taken charge of regular train operations on the corridor.Overall, the plan is to have 100 women operators on the line, including the 90 already operating trains on it.Having an entire Metro corridor with women at the controls also marks a significant step towards greater representation of women in operational roles in urban rail transport.Another important feature of Pune Metro's Pink Line is that 30% of its energy requirements are expected to be met through solar power. The project also uses a 750V DC third-rail electrification system, which eliminates the need for overhead wires.Tata Power Renewables has received a contract from Pune IT City Metro Rail Ltd, which operates Pune Metro Line 3, to install a 7.67 MWp rooftop solar project. The installation will cover all 23 stations and the Metro depot. The electricity generated will be used for captive consumption. The project is expected to help reduce the corridor's operating costs and dependence on conventional sources of electricity.With this, Pune Metro joins several transport projects in India, including other Metro systems, that use solar power. For instance, as of 2023, 35% of Delhi Metro's total energy consumption came from renewable sources. This included 30% from its off-site solar power plant in Rewa, Madhya Pradesh, 4% from rooftop solar panels and 1% from the waste-to-energy plant in Ghazipur, Delhi.Outside the Metro network, Cochin International Airport in Kerala became the world's first airport to run entirely on solar power with the commissioning of a 12 MWp solar PV power plant in 2015.The solar power component, therefore, adds another dimension to the Pink Line's approach to energy use and operational efficiency.The Pink Line is also significant for the model through which it has been developed. It is India's first Metro rail project to be implemented under the public-private partnership (PPP) framework of the Centre's New Metro Rail Policy, 2017, which aims to encourage private investment in transport infrastructure.While cities such as Mumbai and Hyderabad have previously developed Metro projects under PPP models, Pune's Pink Line is the first to be implemented under the framework of the 2017 policy.The project was developed by Pune IT City Metro Rail Limited, a special-purpose company established as a joint venture between TRIL Urban Transport Private Limited, part of the Tata Group, and Germany's Siemens, in collaboration with the Pune Metropolitan Region Development Authority.Another technological feature of the Pink Line is its Siemens-supplied Communication-Based Train Control (CBTC) signalling system. While the existing Purple and Aqua lines also use CBTC systems, these are supplied by France's Alstom.According to Siemens, its CBTC system allows trains to communicate continuously with trackside equipment, enabling high-frequency services while maintaining safe distances between trains. It is designed for semi-automated operations, with provision for a future upgrade to fully automated, driverless operations.The technology adds to the corridor's operational capabilities while leaving scope for greater automation in the future.Despite these features and the integration of Hinjawadi into the Metro network, several challenges remain in improving the overall commuting experience in the city, experts say.For instance, despite the Pink Line reportedly recording a ridership of around 50,000 on its very first day, some passengers raised concerns about gaps in first- and last-mile connectivity.According to Tanzeel Allapur, programme associate at Parisar, a Pune-based NGO working on sustainable urban transport since 1995, the administration cannot limit its idea of a good commuting experience to building new Metro lines alone and must focus on improving connectivity to and from Metro stations.“Finding a connecting bus or shared auto, figuring out where to board, and navigating the surroundings of a Metro station all add to the mental effort involved in making that journey. The administration needs to focus on reducing both the physical friction and the cognitive load involved in these transfers,” she told The Times of India.Echoing this view, Jagannarayan Padmanabhan, senior director at Crisil Intelligence, stressed the importance of seamless connectivity rather than simply adding more routes.“Seamless connectivity with PMPML buses, feeder services, autos and shared mobility, supported by integrated ticketing and pedestrian infrastructure, is essential,” he added.Although it is still early days for the Pink Line, improved connectivity and integration with other modes of transport could further build on the benefits it brings to Pune's public transport network.Looking ahead, transport activist Ranjit Gadgil, who heads Parisar, said that with the Pink Line now operational alongside the two existing corridors, authorities must introduce measures to curb private vehicle use to reduce congestion, pollution and road accidents.“With the addition of the Pink Line to the existing two corridors, it is high time the city started implementing measures to curb vehicle use. These could include on-street parking charges, low-emission zones and street designs that prioritise the safety and movement of pedestrians, cyclists and buses rather than allocating more space to motor vehicles,” he added.Ultimately, the Pink Line offers Pune an opportunity to make public transport a more convenient choice for commuters. Its connectivity to Hinjawadi, in particular, could encourage more people working in the IT hub to consider the Metro for their daily journeys.But the real measure of the Pink Line's success will be whether it can persuade more people to leave their cars and two-wheelers behind and make public transport their preferred choice.
Article Summary: PM Modi virtually inaugurated Pune Metro's Pink Line on November 3. The 23.2-km corridor connects Maan, on Pune's northwestern outskirts, with the District Court Metro station in Shivajinagar, central Pune. It is the network's third corridor to open and the first to pass through Hinajwadi, the city's IT hub.

Article Title: Breakthrough HIV drug sees 18 patent filings, may delay affordable generics

NEW DELHI: An unusually high 18 patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir, a breakthrough HIV therapy, have raised concerns that these could prolong market exclusivity, delay affordable generics, keep prices high and restrict patient access. Contesting the move, patient groups and civil society have filed opposition with the regulatory authorities, arguing the applications lack novelty and inventive steps.Lenacapavir, a long-acting injectable, administered twice yearly for both HIV prevention and treatment, a medicine designated as essential by WHO.Last year, US FDA approved Gilead Sciences' lenacapavir as the first and only twice-yearly injectable pre-exposure prophylaxis to reduce sexually acquired HIV. Gilead has filed at least 18 patent pleas till date in India, covering different aspects of it, including the base compound, salt forms, formulations, dosing regimens, compositions, and methods of use."The pattern of filings reflects a systematic strategy to create layered patent protection around a single medicine, with the effect of deterring generic entry and prolonged monopoly control beyond the standard 20-year patent term.Such practices, also referred to as "evergreening", whereby multiple secondary patents covering minor variations in forms, formulations, or used or pursued to extend exclusivity," KM Gopakumar, senior researcher and legal advisor at TWN told TOI.In a letter to the department for promotion of industry and internal trade, patient groups demanded that the patent office must rigorously examine and reject the company's secondary patent applications.Dr Reddy's is one of six generic manufacturers which has signed voluntary licenses with Gilead to manufacture and commercialise lenacapavir across 120 low and lower middle income countries, including India. The generic injection is projected to cost approximately $40 per person annually. So, apart from the voluntary licence holders, no other generics can manufacture and market the drug.Further, the patents, if granted, are set to expire in 2042, 28 years after the first application was filed. "Granting these patents would legitimise Gilead's evergreening strategy," Prathibha Sivasubramanian of Working Group on Access to Medicines and Treatments, told TOI.
Article Summary: An unusually high 18 patent applications filed in India for lenacapavir, a breakthrough HIV therapy. Concerns that these could prolong market exclusivity, delay affordable generics, keep prices high and restrict patient access. Article Title: After EASA concern, Air India asks crew to remain on board till replacement arrives during Europe fuelling halts
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America that take a fuelling halt in Europe since the US-Iran war broke out this Feb, to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them to operate the remaining lag of the flight. The reason: Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers for the process and since passengers remain on board during this time, cabin crew has to be there to announce precautions like keeping seat belts off.There were some instances when the incoming crew left the aircraft immediately on arrival in Europe. This gap in standard operating procedure (SOP) was detected primarily at Vienna during “EU ramp inspection programme” carried out to do “safety assessment of foreign aircraft” (SAFA). Along with cabin condition issues, this led to European Union Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) SAFA score of Air India rising to 2.7, indicating safety-related deficiencies.The same was conveyed to the Indian Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), which then swung into action along with AI to rectify the situation. The airline started deploying new or retrofitted aircraft on these routes which largely took care of cabin issues.For fuelling, AI asked its crew to remain on board till the replacement crew arrives.After taking these two steps, AI’s SAFA score has now gone to about 1.4, indicating that the issues that led to the earlier higher score have been largely addressed. “The DGCA did extensive monitoring and ensured AI followed the protocol to a T. Now AI is in the ‘good zone’ of Europe’s SAFA with the score falling from 2.7 earlier to about 1.4,” said people in the know. “Now crew often remains on board for about 1-1.5 hours after landing to oversee the fuelling process till relief crew arrives,” they add.AI’s improved SAFA score comes as a breather for the short-staffed DGCA that has been headed by non-aviation generalists for about two decades now, just ahead of facing an audit by the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) from next week. It is also a relief for Air India as it is the only Indian carrier that flies to the US and will be examined closely by FAA for that reason. In operational terms, this should lead to less checks during fuelling stops in Europe and fewer delays on that count during halts there for AI.Refuelling: The SOP is that an engineering team and/or pilots should be in the flight deck when an aircraft is getting refuelled to coordinate with the fuelling staff. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on when fuelling is taking place.The AI circular for pilots, reiterating the incoming set remains on board till it’s replaced by the relief crew. “Before commencing fuelling, the flight deck crew will be informed by engineering. If flight crew are unable to attend the flight deck during refueling, they shall request a qualified engineer to attend the flight deck,” says his circular.It adds: “NO PED (personal electronic devices) NO SMOKING / NO DEVICES / EXIT signs shall be illuminated as an indication to the cabin crew that fuelling is in progress. 'Seat belt' sign must be off. Known high energy equipment such as HF radios shall not be operated (during refuelling).”
Article Summary: Air India has asked its cockpit and cabin crew operating flights between India and North America to remain on board till the relief crew takes over from them. Refuelling takes place during these halts which requires the cockpit to be manned by pilots and/or engineers. The cabin crew has to announce that passengers must not have their seat belts on during fuelling.

NEW DELHI: Taking advantage of liberal laws abroad to obtain a divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law, Supreme Court has ruled.Viewing negatively the use in a foreign court of grounds for divorce which are not recognised in India, SC said a person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist under Indian law, reports Amit Anand Choudhary.With many men approaching a foreign court to get a divorce on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage - despite the wife opposing the plea - and thereafter remarrying, SC said the person has to face proceedings even in a case where he had become a citizen of a foreign country. The top court said legal consequences stemm-ing from the subsisting marriage cannot be overridden by a subsequent change in a spouse's nationality.The bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar allowed criminal proceedings for bigamy against a man who remarried after getting a divorce order from a foreign court on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage in proceedings opposed by the wife.The court said that irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a ground for divorce in Indian law and, therefore, the divorce granted by the foreign court is not valid.“In our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily. This violates the legal threshold of Section 13 of the CPC, which every foreign decree has to pass through,” the SC bench said.The bench also said that if the foreign decree does not satisfy the requirements of Section 13 of the Civil Procedure Code, then the husband, relying on such a decree, cannot be permitted to contend that his first marriage stood dissolved in the eyes of matrimonial laws of India and, thus, escape the rigours of Section 494 of IPC (marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife).“Now, coming to the argument of the husband that since he was a British citizen when the second marriage with second wife was solemnised and since the second marriage took place outside India, keeping in view the mandate of Section 4 of the IPC, he cannot be held liable. We cannot accept this submission in the manner canvassed as the husband was married to first wife in India under Hindu rites, rituals and customs; thus, even if the second marriage took place outside India, the allegations under Section 494 of the IPC cannot be said to be diluted since enquiry for the offence of bigamy cannot be confined to the place of second marriage but must necessarily take into account the subsisting matrimonial relationship. ..” the bench said.The court, however, quashed criminal proceedings against the parents and second wife of the man.
Article Summary: Supreme Court rules that divorce for a wedding solemnised in India will not automatically lead to dissolution of the marriage under Indian law. A person who contracts a second marriage on that basis may face prosecution for bigamy as the first marriage continues to subsist.

NEW DELHI: Telangana BJP president N Ramchander Rao on Saturday claimed that he and other party leaders had been placed under house arrest to prevent them from holding peaceful protests against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's visit to Hyderabad and the Bharat Summit being hosted by the state government.Rao described the action as illegal and said it violated the democratic right to protest. But, Congress is openly crushing democracy and the spirit of Constitution by putting opposition leaders under house arrest in Congress-ruled Telangana," he said.The BJP leader also described the event as an "Anti-Bharat Summit", alleging that the Congress was bringing "anti-national forces" to the state under the guise of the gathering.According to the BJP Telangana State PRO, Rao was placed under house arrest at his residence in Tarnaka, Hyderabad, after calling for the cancellation of the summit and opposing Rahul Gandhi's visit.Rao further alleged that the Congress government was wasting taxpayers' money by organising the event to relaunch Rahul Gandhi politically.Telangana BJP chief spokesperson N V Subhash demanded that the government end Rao's house arrest and release BJP and Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha (BJYM) activists who, he claimed, had been illegally detained.There was no immediate response from the police or the state government to Rao's allegations.Meanwhile, Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao, also known as KTR, criticised Rahul Gandhi's participation in the Bharat Summit, alleging that the Congress leader had remained silent on several issues in Telangana.In a post on X on Friday, KTR accused Rahul Gandhi of not responding to protests by students demanding jobs, the alleged mistreatment of tribal women in Lagacharla and the demolition of houses by the Hyderabad Disaster Response and Asset Protection Agency (HYDRAA)."You didn’t show up when students demanding jobs (that you promised) were being throttled & getting beaten up by Congress police. You were unperturbed when tribal women of Lagacharla were beaten, disrobed & molested for their lands. When Hydraa bulldozers were destroying homes of hardworking Telangana people, you were sleeping in Delhi," he wrote.KTR also raised concerns over the felling of trees at Kancha Gachibowli, alleged damage to KBR Park, the reported defection of 10 BRS MLAs to the Congress and an incident involving women legislators outside the Assembly.He further referred to alleged farmer and weaver suicides, arrests of journalists, land grabbing and corruption allegations against Congress MLAs and ministers.Questioning the purpose of Rahul Gandhi's visit, KTR alleged that the summit was a publicity exercise being funded with public money. He claimed that Rs 100 crore of Telangana taxpayers' money was being spent on the event.Rahul Gandhi was in Hyderabad to attend the Bharat Summit, being held at the Hyderabad International Convention Centre on November 13 and 14, and address a rally of gig workers.According to PTI, he participated in a bike rally with gig workers before addressing them on Saturday. He dedicated the gig workers' welfare legislation enacted by the Telangana government to the workers, describing them as the foundation of the economy and partners in progress.Rahul Gandhi said the Congress had fulfilled its promise of providing social security and protection to gig workers through the legislation. He also accused the BJP and RSS of pursuing an ideology that benefited big industrialists such as Adani and Ambani while treating workers like bonded labourers.Under the Telangana Platform Based Gig Workers (Registration, Social Security and Welfare) Bill, 2026, gig workers are entitled to Rs 5 lakh in accident insurance and Rs 10 lakh in health insurance. The government will also provide Wi-Fi-enabled rest zones, he said.The Telangana government enacted the legislation in March this year after Rahul Gandhi highlighted gig workers' concerns during his Bharat Jodo Yatra. Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, cabinet colleagues and other Congress leaders were present at the rally.
Article Summary: Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) working president KT Rama Rao, also known as KTR, criticised Rahul Gandhi's participation in the Bharat Summit. NEW DELHI: BJP on Saturday urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and his mother, Sonia Gandhi , to return 51 cartons of correspondence belonging to former Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru to the Prime Ministers' Museum and Library (PMML), alleging that the documents were taken away from the institution in 2008.BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan made the appeal on Nehru's birth anniversary, saying the letters formed part of India's documentary heritage and should be available to researchers and the public through the museum.In a post on X, Kesavan questioned why the documents had not been returned and invoked Rahul Gandhi's frequently used slogan, "Daro Mat" (Do not be afraid), asking him to ensure their return."At least on Nehru’s birth anniversary today, will Rahul Gandhi and the Congress first family have the courage to stop acting contrary to the national interest and return the 51 cartons containing Nehru’s correspondence which rightfully belong to the country?" Kesavan said.He added that the correspondence included letters exchanged between Nehru and Edwina Mountbatten, as well as communications with other prominent individuals. Kesavan alleged that the Congress leadership's failure to return the papers would strengthen suspicions about why they were withdrawn from the institution."These letters are a part of the country’s documentary heritage and not somebody’s private property and need to be given back to the Prime Ministers’ Museum and Library (PMML)," he said.Kesavan claimed that the documents had been donated to the Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in 1971 but were taken back by Sonia Gandhi in May 2008, when the Congress-led United Progressive Alliance (UPA) was in power. He also questioned the absence of any mention of the matter in her recent memoir.The dispute over the custody of Nehru's papers has continued for several years. In September 2024, Rizwan Kadri, a member of the PMML Society, wrote to Sonia Gandhi seeking the return of the 51 cartons or permission to digitise the documents and obtain scanned copies for research.Kadri said the material came from around eight sections of the Nehru collection and included correspondence between Nehru and Edwina Mountbatten, as well as letters exchanged with former Union minister Govind Ballabh Pant, socialist leader Jayaprakash Narayan and others.In 2025, Kadri also approached Rahul Gandhi, requesting the return of the documents and describing them as an important part of India's history.The Union ministry of culture clarified in December 2025 that the papers could not be described as missing because their whereabouts were known. Culture minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat had also said that "no document related to the first PM for the country is missing from PMML".In a post on X, the ministry said the documents had been taken back in 2008 following a request made on Sonia Gandhi's behalf. It cited a letter dated April 29, 2008, from M V Rajan, her representative, stating that she wished to take back Nehru's private family letters and notes."Accordingly, 51 cartons of Nehru Papers were sent to Smt. Sonia Gandhi in 2008," the ministry said, adding that PMML had remained in correspondence with her office over their return.It also cited letters sent to Sonia Gandhi's office on January 28 and July 3, 2025, as part of its efforts to retrieve the papers.The ministry said the documents formed part of the country's documentary heritage and that their custody with PMML, along with access for citizens and scholars, was important.Meanwhile, Rahul Gandhi paid tribute to Nehru on his birth anniversary, describing him as the "jewel of India" and saying his vision of a modern, scientific and progressive country continued to inspire the Congress.In a post on X, the leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha said Nehru viewed freedom as the beginning of a new national journey and believed that democracy required citizens' participation and responsibility."India was a quest, an idea for them; diversity as its strength, democracy as its faith, and equality as its foundation," Rahul said, adding that efforts to build the India Nehru had envisioned were a true tribute to him.Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra described Nehru as "a revolutionary, a visionary and a builder". She said the fact that he continued to be criticised more than six decades after his death reflected his commitment to India's Constitution and democracy.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also paid tribute, recalling Nehru's contributions to building a modern and democratic nation. He highlighted Nehru's faith in equality, secularism and scientific thinking, as well as his commitment to children's education.Nehru was born on November 14, 1889, in Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh. He became India's first prime minister after independence on August 15, 1947, and died on May 27, 1964. His birth anniversary is observed as Children's Day in India.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson CR Kesavan made the appeal on Nehru's birth anniversary. Kesavan claimed the documents had been donated to the Nehru Memorial Museum and Library in 1971. He said they were taken back by Sonia Gandhi in May 2008, when Congress-led UPA was in power.

Article Title: AIIMS plans national registry to track poisoning cases

NEW DELHI: AIIMS New Delhi is planning a national system to track poisoning cases across the country, with a proposed National Poisoning Registry that would collect reports of poisoning cases and digitally link poison-control units for real-time reporting.The proposal envisages transforming the National Poisons Information Centre (NPIC) from a 24x7 telephone advisory service into a national nodal network for toxicology, with satellite units connected digitally to the AIIMS centre.Under the proposed system, poisoning cases reported by participating centres could feed into a central database to track emerging trends and improve preparedness. The plan also includes a national antidote bank, analytical testing facility, research and development, real-time reporting software and AI-assisted diagnostic support.Established at AIIMS in 1995, NPIC was India’s first centre of its kind. From a telephone service guiding doctors on emergency poison management, it has grown into a 24x7 toxicology resource receiving calls nationwide. It received over 65,000 calls between 1995 and 2025, involving household products, pesticides, drug overdoses and snake bites.NPIC data show a wide range of exposures, including drugs, agricultural and industrial chemicals, plants, household products and stings and bites.Snake bites were the largest component of sting-and-bite calls in both 2010–19 and 2020–25.The proposed expansion is aimed at moving beyond individual emergency calls to create a broader national picture of poisoning patterns. AIIMS has proposed digitally linking the nodal centre with satellite units, along with analytical testing and a national antidote bank, to strengthen the response to poisoning emergencies.The proposal also seeks wider poison-awareness and capacity-building programmes for children, teachers, parents and occupational workers, along with a National Outreach and Awareness Programme and a dedicated National Poison Awareness Day. As part of the expansion, AIIMS has proposed renaming NPIC as the National Nodal Centre for Toxicological Sciences & Research (NNCTSR).Prof D.S. Arya, Head, Department of Pharmacology and Chief, NPIC, AIIMS, New Delhi, and the team led by Dr Swati Sharma, Senior Scientist and Nodal Officer, NPIC Expansion Programme, Department of Pharmacology, AIIMS, New Delhi.
Article Summary: AIIMS New Delhi is planning a national system to track poisoning cases across the country. A proposed National Poisoning Registry would collect reports of poisoning cases and digitally link poison-control units for real-time reporting. The plan also includes a national antidote bank, analytical testing facility, research and development.

NEW DELHI: Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has conducted searches at 33 locations across six states at the premises of the panel operators of the illegal online betting platform of Mahadev Online Book app in the last few days. The searches were carried out on the basis of disclosures made by the key accused Sourabh Chandrakar, one of the principal promoters of the platform, after his extradition from the Sultanate of Oman.During these searches, live betting and gambling panels were found running and were dismantled. Digital devices, mobile phones and incriminating documents showing the use of mule accounts and a hawala network have been recovered and seized.Cities where searches conducted are Amritsar, Delhi, Nagaur, Dholpur, Bhopal, Raipur, Durg, Indore, Ahmedabad, Vadodara, Surat, Mumbai and Nagpur.Sourabh Chandrakar was extradited from Oman and arrested by CBI on Nov 1. The Special Judge (CBI Cases), Raipur granted his 8 day police custody to CBI. His interrogation revealed the details about the working of the platform and its network of panel operators in India.He was also confronted with the documentary and digital evidence collected during investigation.It may be recalled that CBI has registered two FIRs in the Mahadev Online Book after being transferred from the State Govt. of Chhattisgarh.Investigation conducted so far has revealed that the platform is run from abroad through a Head Office and operates in India through a large network of panel operators. These operators handle customer IDs, collect betting money in the bank accounts exclusively opened or hired in the names of other persons, and send the profits abroad through hawala channels.On expiry of police custody, Sourabh Chandrakar was produced before the Ld. Special Judge (CBI Cases), Raipur on 12.11.2026 and has been remanded to judicial custody till 19.11.2026.Investigation is continuing into the role of the other accused, including those located abroad, the persons who facilitated the operations and the public servants concerned. Steps for extradition of the other absconding accused are under way.Members of the public are cautioned that online betting and gambling are illegal. Lending or renting one's bank account, SIM card or identity documents to others for such activity is also a criminal offence and exposes the account holder to prosecution.
Article Summary: Sourabh Chandrakar was extradited from Oman and arrested by CBI on Nov 1. The Special Judge (CBI Cases), Raipur granted his 8 day police custody to CBI. His interrogation revealed the details about the working of the platform and its network of panel operators.
